LESSON: SIGN READING 15.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: CONSERVING RESOURCES Suggested vocabulary to be signed: waste, save, careful, sh
Topic 15.2: Sign reading 15.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign reading 15.2.1 Fluency, part of CONSERVING RESOURCES Suggested vocabulary to be signed: waste, save, careful, sh in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: where he or she sign reads some lines or stanzas of a poem. Why are punctuation marks important in reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign reading 15.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: The learner learns independently as they practise reading sentences containing decodable and non- decodable words.

• Communication: Singing skills are enhanced as the learner develops fluent sign reading skills.

Values:
Integrity: Discipline is enhanced as the learner conserves resources prudently.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Integrity is developed as the learner uses resources responsibly.

Link to other Learning Areas

Learner is able to relate the skill of sign reading fluently in all learning areas.
